readmeMarkdown:
# agy-standards [Google Antigravity](https://antigravity.google) (`agy`) plugin bundling global rules, lifecycle skills, and language-specific standards. > *"Building the wrong thing is still a waste even when building is faster."* — [Gergely Orosz, LDX3 New York 2026](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uErdlVHb8ow) > > *"The old system scaled consistency. The new system must scale intent."* — [Katie Dill, Stripe](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GLvFTMtw4Jk) *In the era of AI coding, I still plan, write it down, and review the code. Some people run 4–6 agents in parallel—my brain has a concurrency limit of 1.* --- ## Approach `agy-standards` structures development with `agy` around one habit: **agree on what you want to build and put it in writing before any code exists.** That written record replaces long chat histories, where requirements get lost, and takes two forms: - **Specifications (`docs/spec/`)**: Living requirements and design documents that describe how the project works (CLI flags, APIs, configuration, and behavior). - **Issues**: Small, well-defined tasks that describe what needs to change, the edge cases to handle, and how to test it. Each coding or review step can then start in a fresh session and read what it needs from these files. *(See [docs/philosophy.md](docs/philosophy.md) for why the workflow is built this way.)* --- ## Workflow ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Upfront ["Upfront design"] Spec["Spec
(/standards:00-spec)"] -.-> Roadmap["Roadmap
(/standards:01-roadmap)"] end subgraph Daily ["Daily development loop"] Plan["Plan mode
(/plan)"] --> Issue["Issue
(/standards:02-issue)"] --> Code["Implement
(/standards:03-implement)"] end subgraph Ship ["Release pipeline"] Docs["Docs
(/standards:04-docs)"] --> Audit["Audit
(/standards:05-audit)"] --> Release["Release
(/standards:06-release)"] end Roadmap -.->|"New project / module / epic"| Plan Code -->|"Next issue"| Plan Code -->|"Ready to ship"| Docs ``` 1. **Upfront design (`/standards:00-spec`, `/standards:01-roadmap`, as needed)**: - **Write or update specs (`/standards:00-spec`)**: Create or update `docs/spec/` when starting a new project, adding a module, designing a large feature/change, or documenting existing code. - **Slice a large spec (`/standards:01-roadmap`)**: When a new or updated spec is too large for one PR, split the work into ordered vertical slices (`docs/roadmap.md` on an integration branch), then run the **Daily development loop** once per slice. 2. **Daily development loop (`Plan` $\rightarrow$ `/standards:02-issue` $\rightarrow$ `/standards:03-implement`)**: - **Plan (`--mode plan` / `/plan`)**: Discuss the problem and agree on the approach before touching code (or select the next `Pending` roadmap slice when inside an epic). - **Create issue (`/standards:02-issue`)**: Turn the agreed plan or roadmap slice into a structured issue draft (`.issue-draft.md`) with acceptance criteria, edge cases, and test cases. - **Implement (`/standards:03-implement`)**: Create a topic branch (off the default branch, or off the integration branch for epic slices), update `docs/spec/` and the code together, run tests and linters, and open a PR. Once all epic slices merge, remove `docs/roadmap.md` and merge the integration branch into `main`. 3. **Release pipeline (`/standards:04-docs` $\rightarrow$ `/standards:05-audit` $\rightarrow$ `/standards:06-release`)**: When ready to release, review user docs, run a read-only audit across specs, code, and tests, and cut the release tag. *(For a step-by-step example of how a full session looks in practice, see [docs/walkthrough.md](docs/walkthrough.md).)* ### Companion tool: [`git-brx`](https://github.com/bvarnai/git-brx) (optional) `agy-standards` shapes how the agent plans, writes specs, codes, audits, and writes commits. `git-brx` serves a different purpose in the same workflow: it covers your side of it. It brings its own branching conventions and turns them into concrete commands (`git brx create`, `sync`, `publish`, `review`, and so on) on top of Git, so you can follow the workflow without being fluent in Git. It also ships its own agent skill; see its [AI agent integration guide](https://github.com/bvarnai/git-brx/blob/main/docs/user-guide/getting-started.md). If `git-brx` is on `PATH`, the agent uses it for branches, syncing, and PRs. If not, the agent follows the project's own conventions. ### Working effectively - **Use plan mode as an interview.** Give a rough 2-sentence idea and ask `agy` to challenge the edge cases and trade-offs. Answering a few sharp questions triggers the same design thinking that used to happen while coding by hand. Then let `/standards:00-spec` or `/standards:02-issue` draft the Markdown from your answers. - **Prototype when the design isn't clear yet.** Build a rough, throwaway version to learn what works, then write the real design into `docs/spec/`. - **Use the fast path for trivial changes.** Small fixes, doc edits, and dependency bumps don't need an issue. --- ## Repository organization ```text agy-standards/ ├── plugin.json # Native agy plugin manifest ├── assets/logo.svg # Monochrome plugin mark ├── rules/ # Universal always-on rule entrypoint │ └── GEMINI.md # @-imports fragments + formatting & tool policy ├── standards/ # Stack-specific standards (routed via fragments/stack-routing.md) │ ├── go.md # Go architecture, error wrapping, concurrency & testing │ ├── python.md # Python CLI/service architecture, strict typing, ruff/mypy/pytest │ ├── java.md # Modern Java idioms, null-safety, Maven/Gradle verification │ ├── embedded.md # Embedded C/C++ deterministic memory, ISR safety, HAL │ └── shell.md # Bash/Shell naming (kebab-case CLI), safety, shellcheck & Bats ├── skills/ # Lifecycle slash commands (/standards:00-spec .. /standards:06-release) │ └── /SKILL.md # Skill definition (+ templates/ where applicable) └── fragments/ # Shared rule & prompt fragments (spec-driven, git, stack-routing, tone) ``` --- ## Universal lifecycle skills Run these skills inside an interactive `agy` session (assuming the plugin is linked as `standards`): | Stage | Slash command | When to run | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **0. Spec** | `/standards:00-spec` | New project, module, or big change | Author or update technical specs in `docs/spec/`. | | **1. Roadmap** | `/standards:01-roadmap` | Spec too large for a single PR | Partition `docs/spec/` into vertical slices on an integration branch. | | **2. Issue** | `/standards:02-issue` | Each PR (standalone or slice) | Draft strict, spec-driven issues. | | **3. Implement** | `/standards:03-implement` | Every PR | Implement features/fixes with spec sync & tests. | | **4. Docs** | `/standards:04-docs` | Before release | Audit docs for tone and factual accuracy. | | **5. Audit** | `/standards:05-audit` | Before release | Read-only pre-release readiness checklist. | | **6. Release** | `/standards:06-release` | When cutting a tag | Prepare changelog/manifests and tag default branch. | ### Model & effort mental compass Start your `agy` session in **Build** (`medium`) as the default, then shift up to **Design** (`high`) or down to **Ship** (`low`) when the stage calls for it: | Gear | When to use | Stages | Model profile | Effort & mode | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **1. Design** | Designing architecture, slicing epics, catching subtle drift, or stuck on a hard bug | `00-spec`, `01-roadmap` | Strongest reasoning model | `high` *(+ `plan` for `00-spec`, `01-roadmap`)* | | **2. Build** *(default)* | Day-to-day coding, tests, issue drafting, and doc reviews | `02-issue`, `03-implement`, `04-docs` | Fast, surgical coding model | `medium` | | **3. Ship** | Deterministic checklists and release steps where deep reasoning adds latency | `05-audit`, `06-release` | Fastest available (or same model) | `low` | For concrete model picks and per-stage rationale, see [docs/models.md](./docs/models.md). --- ## Multi-stack domain rule routing Always-on [`fragments/stack-routing.md`](fragments/stack-routing.md) (imported by [`rules/GEMINI.md`](rules/GEMINI.md)) inspects the current working directory (`CWD`) during planning, issue drafting, implementation, and auditing to load the matching standard: - **Go**: Triggered by `go.mod` $\rightarrow$ enforces [standards/go.md](standards/go.md) (`go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...`). - **Python**: Triggered by `pyproject.toml` / `setup.py` / `requirements.txt` $\rightarrow$ enforces [standards/python.md](standards/python.md) (`ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `mypy` / `pyright`, `pytest`). - **Java**: Triggered by `pom.xml` / `build.gradle` / `build.gradle.kts` $\rightarrow$ enforces [standards/java.md](standards/java.md) (`./mvnw test` / `./gradlew check`). - **Embedded C/C++**: Triggered by `CMakeLists.txt` / `platformio.ini` / `Kconfig` / `*.ld` / `Makefile` (firmware) $\rightarrow$ enforces [standards/embedded.md](standards/embedded.md) (deterministic memory, fixed-width types, ISR safety). - **Shell / Bash**: Triggered by `*.sh` / `*.bats` / `.bashrc.d/` / `bin/` $\rightarrow$ enforces [standards/shell.md](standards/shell.md) (`kebab-case` public interfaces, `shellcheck`, `bats`). To add a new stack (e.g. Rust, TypeScript), create `standards/.md` and add one row to `fragments/stack-routing.md`. --- ## Configuring Antigravity (`agy`) `agy-standards` is packaged as a native Antigravity plugin (`plugin.json`). - **Install from GitHub (`agy` >= 1.5.11):** ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/bvarnai/agy-standards ``` - **Install from a local clone (symlink):** Linking the repository into `~/.gemini/config/plugins/` registers both the global rules (`rules/`) and all lifecycle skills (`skills/`) with a single directory symlink: ```bash mkdir -p ~/.gemini/config/plugins ln -sfn "" ~/.gemini/config/plugins/standards ``` --- ## 🤖 AI Disclosure ![AI Assisted](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI-Assisted-blue?style=flat-square) This project was developed with the assistance of AI tools. All AI-generated code has been reviewed, tested, and manually refined.
